0.headline: IPO action: Rs 7,700 crore worth 9 IPOs to hit Dalal Street, 8 new listings scheduled next week
0.heading: IPO action: Rs 7,700 crore worth 9 IPOs to hit Dalal Street, 8 new listings scheduled next week
0.intro: This included five maiden public issues amounting to Rs 7,479 crore from the mainboard segment, and the remainder four offers worth Rs 203 crore from the SME segment.
0.body:
The relentless action will continue in the primary market in the next week, too, starting from August 10 as nearly Rs 7,700 crore worth nine new IPOs will be available for investment along side eight companies lined up for their market debut.

This included five maiden public issues amounting to Rs 7,479 crore from the mainboard segment, and the remainder four offers worth Rs 203 crore from the SME segment.

The week will be starting with Dhoot Transmission, and Molbio Diagnostics IPOs which are set to open for public subscription on August 10 and close on August 12.

Bain Capital-backed Dhoot Transmission, the Maharashtra-based electrical and electronics company that manufactures wiring harnesses and electrical distribution systems for automotive and non-automotive applications, is planning to raise Rs 3,066.9 crore via initial public offering (IPO) at the upper end of price band of Rs 829-871 per share.

The IPO included fresh issuance of shares worth Rs 1,400 crore, while promoters - Bain Capital-owned BC Asia InvestmentsXV, and Mangalam Capital, will be selling 1.6 crore shares and 31.18 lakh shares, respectively via offer-for-sale (OFS), amounting to Rs 1,666.9 crore.

Goa-based point-of-care molecular diagnostics company Molbio Diagnostics is raising Rs 939.70 crore via maiden public issue which included issuance of fresh shares worth Rs 200 crore, and an OFS of 91.66 lakh shares worth Rs 739.70 crore. The Temasek, Motilal Oswal-backed company has fixed price band at Rs 768-807 per share.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Both Dhoot Transmission, and Molbio Diagnostics already raised Rs 918 crore, and 281 crore via anchor book on August 7, a day before their offer opening for public subscription.

This followed by Milky Mist Dairy Food, the Tamil Nadu-based dairy products maker, which will launch its Rs 1,553-crore public issue on August 11 with price band at Rs 133-140 per share. The IPO is a combination of fresh issue of Rs 1,428 crore, and an OFS of Rs 125 crore worth shares by promoters Sathishkumar T, and his wife Anitha S.

Shiprocket, and Behari Lal Engineering will be the last two IPOs from the mainboard segment for the next week, opening both on August 12 and close on August 14.

Shiprocket, a technology-led e-commerce enablement platform that helps MSMEs and large retailers manage online commerce, aims to mobilise Rs 1,617.5 crore via public issue at the higher end of price band of Rs 92-97 apiece.

The fresh issue component will fetch the Bertelsmann-, Temasek-, Tribe Capital-backed Gurugram-based company Rs 885.50 crore, while investors and other existing shareholders will offload shares worth Rs 732 crore through an OFS.

Behari Lal Engineering, the Delhi-based iron and steel manufacturer, will be the smallest IPO in size amongst them, mobilising Rs 301.62 crore through the IPO, comprising a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 93 crore and an OFS of 73.2 lakh shares worth Rs 208.62 crore. The price band for the offer has been fixed at Rs 271-285 per share.

In the SME segment, Fascinate Textiles, and Sham Foam will be the first amongst four companies, both opening their IPOs on August 11.

Ready-made garments manufacturer Fascinate Textiles is planning to mobilise Rs 67 crore via public issue at the upper end of price band of Rs 148-156 per share, while Sham Foam that makes polyurethane foam, mattresses and other allied home comfort products approached capital markets with a fixed price issue, raising Rs 40.5 crore at Rs 130 per share.

This followed by Pramodini Medicare, and Q&amp;T Foods which will open their IPOs for public subscription on August 12.

Andhra Pradesh-based diagnostic service provider Pramodini Medicare has fixed price band at Rs 110-118 per share for its initial share sale worth Rs 69.04 crore which comprises of fresh issue of 53.5 lakh shares worth Rs 63.13 crore, and an offer-for-sale of 5 lakh shares amounting to Rs 5.9 crore.

Q&amp;T Foods, the Uttar Pradesh-based bakery products maker, tapped capital markets to mobilise Rs 26.24 crore by issuing 22.82 lakh shares via IPO at a fixed price of Rs 115 per share.

Meanwhile, supply chain and asset-pooling solutions provider LEAP India, and water &amp; wastewater infrastructure development company Technocraft Ventures will close their maiden public issues on August 11. Both mainboard IPOs, which opened on August 7, saw 26 percent, and 2.59 times subscription, respectively.

In the SME segment, auto parts maker LAPL Automotive will close its maiden public issue on August 10, while the offer by film production company Optimystix Entertainment India will remain open till August 11. LAPL saw 29.28 times subscription in the last two days, while Optimystix witnessed 63 percent subscription on its debut day.

On the listing front, Ardee Industries with a focus on recycling of end-of-life energy storage products and non-ferrous scrap will list its equity shares on the exchanges on August 12, followed by Technocraft Ventures, and LEAP India which are scheduled for their market debut on August 14.

Telecom towers manufacturer Anawil Wire &amp; Engineering will be the first from the SME segment listing on August 10, followed by solar panel cleaning robot maker Aegeus Technologies on August 11, and GV Electricals, the power distribution infrastructure service provider, on August 12.

Further, LAPL Automotive will make its market debut on August 13, while Optimystix Entertainment India will be the last from the SME section, listing its shares on August 14.

1.headline: Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust files IPO papers, likely to raise Rs 6,000 crore
1.heading: Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust files IPO papers, likely to raise Rs 6,000 crore
1.intro: Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust IPO | The InvIT proposed to raise Rs 500 crore by issuing fresh units, along side an offer-for-sale of 30.47 crore units by existing unitholders.
1.body:
Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust, India's second-largest telecom tower operator, has filed draft offer documents with the markets regulator to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO) and transition from a privately listed infrastructure investment trust (InvIT) to a publicly listed InvIT.

The telecom tower InvIT plans to raise Rs 500 crore through a fresh issue of units, alongside an offer-for-sale (OFS) of up to 30.47 crore units by existing unitholders, according to the draft papers filed on August 6.

Under the OFS, Brookfield Corporation-managed BIF IV Jarvis India will sell up to 18.86 crore units, GIC affiliate Anahera Investment will offload up to 7.65 crore units, while Rossland IMC Limited Partnership will sell up to 3.96 crore units.

Moneycontrol was the first to report that Brookfield-sponsored Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust plans to file draft papers for a Rs 6,000-crore initial public offering (IPO).

The InvIT plans to use the net proceeds from the fresh issue to invest in its portfolio assets and fund capital expenditure requirements. The remaining proceeds will be used for general purposes. Proceeds from the OFS will accrue to the selling unitholders.

2.58 lakh telecom sites

Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust owns 2.58 lakh telecom sites, including macro towers, rooftop structures, in-building solutions and outdoor small cells.

The InvIT has 3.15 lakh tenancies across all 22 telecom circles, giving it an approximately 39 percent market share by sites and 34 percent by tenancies, according to the draft papers.

Its privately traded units have gained 1.18 percent so far in the current quarter to Rs 171.50 on the BSE, after rising 8.65 percent in the quarter ended June 2026 to Rs 169.50.

Brookfield holds 54.36% stake

Brookfield Asset Management holds a 54.36 percent stake in Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust through its affiliates BIF IV Jarvis India and Project Holdings Nine (DIFC).

Anahera Investment holds 22.06 percent, or 67.22 crore units, while BCI IRR India Holdings Inc, backed by British Columbia Investment Management Corporation, owns 9.77 percent, or 29.78 crore units.

Brookfield Asset Management manages more than $1 trillion in assets across infrastructure, real estate, credit, private equity and energy.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Brookfield-controlled Data Link Investment Manager is the investment manager for Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust, while Axis Trustee Services acts as its trustee.

Profit rises 32%

Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust reported a 31.8 percent rise in profit to Rs 1,106.6 crore in FY26, from Rs 839.9 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Revenue increased 24.2 percent to Rs 24,165 crore in FY26 from Rs 19,454 crore a year earlier.

JM Financial, NovaaOne Capital, Ambit, Axis Capital, Citigroup Global Markets India, Investec Capital Services (India), Jefferies India, Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, SBI Capital Markets and 360 ONE WAM have been appointed as merchant bankers for the IPO.

2.headline: IPO-bound Cult founder Rishabh Telang accused of forging co-founder’s signatures; company calls charges false
2.heading: IPO-bound Cult founder Rishabh Telang accused of forging co-founder’s signatures; company calls charges false
2.intro: Bellandur Police registered the FIR on August 6 based on a complaint filed by Deepak Poduval, one of the original co-founders of Cult. In response, Telang called the complaint mala fide, pointing to a legal case filed by his sister, Poduval’s wife, in a property dispute on July 1, 2026. Cult said the consideration was duly paid and acknowledged. It is now contesting the charges
2.body:
IPO-bound Cult founder Rishabh Telang has been accused by his former co-founder and brother-in-law Deepak Poduval of forging Poduval’s signatures on documents used to wind up Cult Fitness Private Limited, the original company behind the Cult brand.

Poduval and Telang founded Cult Fitness in 2015, building the Bengaluru-based fitness chain around group workouts and the Cult brand. The Cult brand later became part of the broader Cult.fit fitness business, which has since expanded into a nationwide fitness platform.

Bellandur Police registered the FIR on August 6, naming Telang and Cult Fitness Private Limited as accused. The FIR alleges forgery, cheating and criminal conspiracy, among other offences.

ALSO READ: Temasek-, Accel-backed fitness platform Cult.Fit files IPO papers to raise up to Rs 950 crore via fresh issue

Cult.fit says the company at the centre of the FIR was separate from its business and that its subsidiary, CultFit Healthcare Private Limited, acquired certain assets and intellectual property from Poduval and Cult Fitness in 2016 under contractual arrangements. Telang has separately denied forging Poduval’s signatures and said Poduval was involved in the transaction and the subsequent winding-up of Cult Fitness.

All of the responses were in response to Moneycontrol's queries.

The dispute is the second recent instance of a co-founder raising allegations of wrongdoing involving a startup ahead of an IPO, after rental furniture startup Rentomojo co-founder and former director Ajay Nain raised concerns over the transfer of his stake and the company’s corporate filings.

The case is yet to be resolved.

FIR alleges forgery

Poduval alleges that documents filed with the Registrar of Companies in 2019 carried forged signatures and were used to wind up Cult Fitness without his authorisation.

He said he found the filings this year while reviewing Cult Fitness’ records on the MCA portal. In a note, Poduval said the documents included filings relating to the company’s strike-off and carried what he alleges were forged versions of his signature.

“The company was struck off later that year, and my entire 50% shareholding was extinguished without a rupee of consideration,” Poduval told Moneycontrol.

Cult.fit’s account

Cult.fit said it had not received any communication from authorities and became aware of the matter through media queries. It also clarified that neither Cult.fit Limited nor its subsidiaries, including CultFit Healthcare Private Limited, is an accused party in the FIR.

“The accused entity, Cult Fitness Private Limited, was a separate independent company of the complainant himself and we did not have any ownership or management control,” the company said.

Cult.fit said its subsidiary acquired certain assets and intellectual property rights, including the ‘Cult - The Workout Station’ brand name, from Poduval and Cult Fitness in 2016 “under appropriate contractual arrangements” and for consideration that was “duly paid and also acknowledged by the complainant”.

“With this, this acquisition stood consummated and closed,” it said.

Telang denies charges

Telang has categorically denied forging Poduval’s signatures and said Poduval was involved in the transactions with CultFit Healthcare as well as the winding-up of Cult Fitness.

“Deepak was fully involved in the transactions with Cultfit Healthcare Pvt. Ltd. as well as the winding up of Cult Fitness Pvt. Ltd., of which I possess multiple correspondence,” Telang said.

He pointed to an MCA email dated March 12, 2020, acknowledging the winding-up of Cult Fitness and said the communication was shared with both him and Poduval.

Telang also said Poduval had received payment from CultFit Healthcare as part of the agreement. Poduval, however, denied this.

“The allegations are entirely without merit, and I remain confident that the facts will emerge through due process,” he said.

Telang also questioned the timing of the FIR, pointing to a property-settlement case filed against Poduval by his sister, who is Poduval’s wife, on July 1, 2026. He said the ongoing case “appears to have triggered the current action”.

"I will also address the allegations made in the FIR in the appropriate legal forum as part of the ongoing court proceedings. The allegations are entirely without merit, and I remain confident that the facts will emerge through due process. Given the serious and defamatory nature of these allegations, I am also evaluating all legal remedies available to protect my reputation," Telang said in his statement.

The allegations in the Cult Fitness FIR are yet to be adjudicated.
